name: Ramanujan-Prony latent decomposer
source_motif: moment/power-sum sequence -> rational generating function -> partial fractions
modern_target: sparse FFT, recurrence discovery, sequence compression, system identification, model distillation
why_exciting: Turns long traces into a small set of hidden poles/weights; directly matches the user intuition of compressed latent representations.
novelty_status: Classical method exists; opportunity is a Ramanujan-style automated compressor that tries rational, q-rational, product, and continued-fraction latent forms across notebook formulas.
next_experiment: Run over formula-generated sequences and score by recovered poles, residual, and extrapolation; compare to Berlekamp-Massey, matrix pencil, sparse FFT, Padé.
risk: Numerically brittle with noise; existing literature extensive.

name: Ramanujan-sum periodicity layer
source_motif: finite trigonometric/Ramanujan sums c_q(n) as divisor-aware basis
modern_target: time-series periodicity, event streams, neural sequence features, anomaly detection, sparse periodic coding
why_exciting: A periodicity basis indexed by integer period/divisibility rather than only Fourier frequency; can reveal hidden cycles at low sample counts.
novelty_status: Signal-processing literature exists; ML/attention/kernel deployment looks underexplored.
next_experiment: Implement differentiable Ramanujan-filter bank and compare against Fourier features on integer-period synthetic and real event data.
risk: May lose to learned Fourier/wavelet features unless tasks have exact arithmetic periods.

name: q-series representation compiler
source_motif: switch among product, sum, recurrence, congruence, modular, and asymptotic coefficient views
modern_target: formal power series, exact combinatorics, symbolic algebra, coefficient extraction, theorem proving benchmarks
why_exciting: The same object has many executable forms; a cost model can pick the cheapest representation for coefficient, residue, or asymptotic queries.
novelty_status: Strong special-case SOTA exists for partitions/modular forms; general compiler for arbitrary Ramanujan-style q-products is less mature.
next_experiment: DSL for q-Pochhammer/eta quotients; query planner chooses DP, recurrence, modular formula, or asymptotic; compare to Sage/FLINT/Mathematica where possible.
risk: Proof/certification and domain recognition are hard.

name: Continued-fraction executable approximants
source_motif: compact continued fractions and product quotients as small stable programs
modern_target: special functions, constants, activation approximants, online filters, kernel compression
why_exciting: A continued fraction is often more stable and state-light than a polynomial/rational approximation.
novelty_status: Ramanujan Machine validates automated CF search; opportunity is function/kernel libraries rather than constants only.
next_experiment: Mine CF templates, fit to target functions, verify with intervals, compare to minimax/Chebyshev/Padé.
risk: Many targets are already well served by minimax approximants.

name: Divisor-rich hardware scheduler
source_motif: integers optimized by divisor lattice/factorization optionality
modern_target: FFT/NTT lengths, GPU tiles, batch/sequence padding, distributed shard sizes
why_exciting: Low-hanging practical payoff: pick sizes that keep many algorithmic decompositions open, not merely powers of two.
novelty_status: Mixed-radix planning is known; explicit HCN-style optionality objective is the recombination.
next_experiment: Benchmark candidate lengths under FFT libraries and GPU kernels with padding costs.
risk: Vendor libraries already encode many heuristics; gains may be workload-specific.

name: Congruence checksums for exact/approximate computation
source_motif: cheap modular invariants and partition congruences
modern_target: large DP, coefficient extraction, computer algebra, theorem prover sanity checks, approximate integer pipelines
why_exciting: Attaches very cheap truth constraints to expensive computations.
novelty_status: Known in computational number theory; useful as modern library engineering.
next_experiment: Wrap generating-function algorithms with residue sentinels; inject errors and measure detection/pruning.
risk: Most useful when algebraic structure is known.

name: Asymptotic + exact-correction kernels
source_motif: dominant asymptotic plus compact correction/error expression
modern_target: special function evaluation, inverse estimates, big coefficient approximations, initialization for solvers
why_exciting: Fast approximate jump followed by a small certified correction; very Ramanujan-like in feel.
novelty_status: Core numerical-analysis pattern; opportunity is a curated Ramanujan-derived catalog with implementation tests.
next_experiment: Build formula cards with regimes, error terms, and code kernels.
